# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** | Top talker in `conv,ip`, source of all outbound activity below |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** | ARP reply for 10.1.21.58; matches DHCP client hardware address |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (NetBIOS aliases WIN11OFFICE / WIN-LU4L24X3UB7, domain `win11office.com`) | NBNS name registration from 10.1.21.58; DHCP `hostname` option; LDAP SRV queries for `WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com` |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString=gwyatt` exchanged between 10.1.21.58 and DC 10.1.21.2 |

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.**

No AV/IDS alerts were included with the evidence and the observed payload transfers are fully TLS-encrypted, so no file hash or static signature could be recovered. Based on traffic behavior, the host was funneled through a **browser-fingerprinting gate/TDS (traffic distribution system)** typical of fake-download / fake-CAPTCHA (ClickFix-style) malware-delivery chains that stage commodity info-stealers. The chain observed:

1. **45.3–48.3s** — DNS lookups for `hiyter.com`, `media.megafilehub4.lat`, then `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (fake file-hosting naming pattern), followed immediately by a **16 MB single TLS stream** from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67) lasting ~22 seconds — consistent with a payload/installer download. Content is TLS-encrypted (Cloudflare-fronted, ECH in use), so no filename or hash could be extracted.
2. **90–92s** — Lookups for `whooptm.cyou` and `whitepepper.su`.
3. **92s onward** — Repeated plaintext HTTP calls from 10.1.21.58 to `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49) hitting `/api/set_agent`, first with `agent=Chrome` then again with `agent=Edge`, each followed by a POST to the same path with `&act=log` carrying an 8KB `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body containing a **full browser fingerprint**: platform/UA, WebGL vendor/renderer, a canvas-fingerprint PNG, screen/hardware profile, installed fonts, audio stack, and plugin list.
4. **122–126s** — Lookups/TLS to `holiday-forever.cc` and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` — naming and behavior consistent with fake "verify you are human" / firewall-check gate pages used in the same class of campaigns.

This fingerprint-collection-then-gate pattern (unique `id`/`token` pair issued per victim, resubmitted per browser identity) is the signature behavior of a **stealer-delivery TDS/anti-bot gate**, not of a specific named stealer family confirmed by static analysis. No host-side artifacts (process, registry, filesystem) were available in this evidence set to confirm a specific strain (e.g., Lumma/Vidar/StealC-class); the family name cannot be asserted with confidence from network traffic alone.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / gate endpoints (IP:port)**
- `153.92.1.49:80` — whitepepper.su (fingerprint-collection/gate HTTP traffic)
- `153.92.1.49:443` — whitepepper.su (TLS)
- `104.21.46.67:443` — arch.filemegahab4.sbs (16 MB payload transfer, Cloudflare-fronted)
- `104.21.48.156:443` — media.megafilehub4.lat
- `62.72.32.156:443` — whooptm.cyou
- `80.97.160.24:443` — holiday-forever.cc
- `104.21.9.36:443` — communicationfirewall-security.cc
- `104.21.22.231:443` — hiyter.com

**Malicious domains**
- whitepepper.su
- arch.filemegahab4.sbs
- media.megafilehub4.lat
- hiyter.com
- whooptm.cyou
- holiday-forever.cc
- communicationfirewall-security.cc

**Malicious URLs (observed in cleartext HTTP)**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST, fingerprint exfil)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log` (POST, fingerprint exfil)

**Files / hashes**
- **None recoverable.** The only substantial binary-sized transfer (16 MB, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, TCP stream 52) is TLS-encrypted end-to-end; `tshark --export-objects` yielded no executable/archive artifacts, only benign objects (`favicon.ico`, `connecttest.txt`, MS component-updater JSON). No filename or SHA256 can be grounded in this capture.

## Benign / Unrelated Context
Standard AD domain-join and workstation chatter tied to `win11office.com`/`mshome.net` (LDAP, Kerberos, DCE/RPC, SMB2, NBNS, mDNS, SSDP, LLMNR), Windows telemetry/update endpoints (`*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `licensing.mp.microsoft.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`), and normal browsing to Google/Microsoft/Bing/MSN/Cloudflare CDN infrastructure.
